input.summary: An attacker at 198.51.100.23 (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL; on threat feeds as bulletproof hosting with an open Docker registry on :5000 and K8s API brute-forcing) used Jordan Doe's (jdoe@example.com) credentials against all three payments-prod clusters while Jordan was on PTO (2026-10-12..19). The client was linux kubectl, but Jordan normally uses macOS (darwin). The same playbook ran on EKS (14:02-14:25), GKE (14:38-15:01) and AKS (15:11-15:34). Steps: a permissions check (selfsubjectrulesreviews) and namespace listing; kube-system secret listing and job creation, which were denied (403); listing payments secrets and reading payments-db-credentials; creating a privileged hostPID/hostNetwork pod with host / mounted (debug-tools-7f9c) and running nsenter into the node's PID 1 to escape onto the node. From the node the attacker took the argocd-application-controller service account token and used it from the same external IP to create a ClusterRoleBinding named jdoe-break-glass, giving jdoe cluster-admin. With cluster-admin, the attacker set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent and a CronJob node-cert-rotate, both pulling images from 198.51.100.23:5000, plus a NodePort service metrics-agent-np on port 30080. The attacker then listed secrets across all namespaces, which is the alerted event.

argocd-application-controller normal activity from in-cluster IP 10.0.12.108 with its own argocd user agent (3840 events); only the 2 calls from 198.51.100.23 using kubectl are malicious

Many SRE/developer interactive execs (sh/bash into app containers) and namespace-scoped db-credential reads from corporate 203.0.113.x egress are routine operations, with no nsenter or privileged pods
daemon-set-controller privileged pod creations in kube-system come from managed DaemonSets
